title: Launcher pair hardening (DEC-282 (a2) review findings on #744)
description: Follow-up to the opus security review of opum-ai/quest-cli#744 (approved at 75dabe81). Must land before the pair cut; lore-cli makes the same changes in #734 round 4 so the wrappers stay one design. N1: CHANGELOG names the wrong baseline (released 0.15.0 exited 1 when the child died by a signal; 128+n was unshipped round-1 code). N2: re-raise every terminating signal Node leaves at default; for SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ, SIGUSR1 exit 128+n instead (SIGUSR1 self-kill opens Node inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229). N3: wrap spawn() in try/catch so a synchronous throw (ENOEXEC, E2BIG) prints the same Quest could not start message, exit 1, no stack. N4: correct the setsid comment (no controlling terminal; SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU reason is wrong). N5: on-TTY test fails rather than skips when CI is set and script is missing; Number.isInteger on both pgids. N6: CHANGELOG residual names QCLI-571 and the TTY residual (on a TTY a SIGTERM reaches the child only, not its grandchildren). Not in scope: a tcgetpgrp-based pair-wide TTY test (design change routed to opum-doc).

acceptanceCriteria.text: CHANGELOG states the real baseline change and no longer lists a spawn-failure exit as a change
A child dying by SIGUSR1 or SIGPIPE makes the wrapper exit 128+n with no Debugger listening on stderr, proven by tests
A synchronous spawn throw (ENOEXEC) prints Quest could not start, exits 1 and prints no stack, proven by a test that goes red without the try/catch
The setsid comment is corrected and the CHANGELOG residual names QCLI-571 and the TTY grandchild residual
The on-TTY test fails when CI is set and script is missing, and both pgids are asserted integers
DEC-282 (a3) item 2: the child owns its process group only when none of fds 0, 1 and 2 is a terminal, proven by a stdin-piped/stdout-on-a-terminal test and an fd-0-only mutant that goes red on it
Review findings F1, F2, F3 and the CHANGELOG nit on #749 are taken
F4: a deterministic SIGUSR1 witness (a --require preload recording the self-kill) replaces stderr text as the only evidence, and the overclaiming comment is corrected

implementationNotes: PREDICTIONS written before the hardening mutants: (M10) spawn() try/catch removed: ONLY the ENOEXEC test goes red (stack trace on stderr). (M11) the NODE_HANDLED early return removed (self-kill for SIGPIPE/SIGXFSZ/SIGUSR1): the SIGUSR1 test goes red (inspector banner on stderr); the SIGPIPE test stays GREEN because Node ignores SIGPIPE, the self-kill does nothing and the 128+n fallback applies - that test pins behaviour, it is not a mutation witness. N5a/N5b/N4/N1/N6 are a CI-fail guard, assertions, a comment and docs: no mutant claimed.

Mutants vs predictions: M10 (try/catch removed) only the ENOEXEC test red - as predicted. M11 (NODE_HANDLED removed) only the SIGUSR1 test red; SIGPIPE stayed green - as predicted. Suite 13 pass. N5a: on-TTY test now fails (expect(hasScript)) when CI is set and script is missing. CI-runner question: the 75dabe81 source-gates job ran on ubuntu-24.04 (workflow runs-on) and its log lists test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts in the bun test command, but the log does not print per-test pass/skip lines, so whether the on-TTY test ran or skipped there is NOT confirmed from the log; with this change a missing script now fails CI instead of skipping. ACs checked on local evidence; CI is the remaining evidence.

CI RED at a9d44797: source-gates failed in the top_level group (exit 1); the prepublish log does not print the failing test, so the cause is INFERRED, not read. Hypothesis: the ENOEXEC test - libuv uses execvp, and glibc execvp retries an ENOEXEC file through /bin/sh, so on ubuntu a text file runs as a script (exit 127) instead of making spawn() throw, while macOS threw. Fix: the throw is now made deterministic with a --require preload that replaces child_process.spawn; the M10 mutant (try/catch removed) still goes red on it. Whether this clears CI is measured only by the next run.

DEC-282 (a3) item 2 built locally (NOT pushed: held until the leader relays the aae541f review verdict). ownGroup only when none of fds 0,1,2 is a terminal; new test runs `: | node wrapper` under script(1) so stdin is a pipe and stdout/stderr the pty, asserting equal pgids; the all-fds-terminal test and the all-piped own-group test are kept. PREDICTION written before the mutant: (M13) ownGroup checking fd 0 only: ONLY the stdin-piped/stdout-on-terminal test goes red; all other 13 stay green.
M13 (fd 0 only) result: ONLY the stdin-piped/stdout-on-terminal test red, 13 pass 1 fail - as predicted; restored 14 pass. Committed locally, not pushed.

#749 landed as approved at aae541fd (origin/dev 98c323a0). Next PR carries (a3) plus F1-F4 and the CHANGELOG nit. PREDICTION before re-measuring M11 (NODE_HANDLED early return removed): the SIGUSR1 test is red, the SIGPIPE test stays green (Node ignores SIGPIPE), all others green; the stronger inspector/9229 assertions are a witness-hardening, not a new mutant.

M11 re-measured with the strengthened witness: SIGUSR1 test red (stderr "Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/..."), SIGPIPE green, 13 pass 1 fail - as predicted; restored 14 pass. F1-F3 and the CHANGELOG nit are comment/doc changes (no mutant). (a3) three-fd group rule rides the same PR; QCLI-572 closes after that PR merges.

VERDICT: APPROVE — opum-ai/quest-cli#750 (QCLI-572) at e448171c, no blocking findings
SHA: e448171c

What I read and how: this is a read-only review and I ran nothing. I read bin/quest.cjs, test/qcli567-wrapper-orphan.test.ts and CHANGELOG.md at the head. I also read the full PR diff, DEC-282 (opum-doc origin/dev text, all of it) and the #749 review at aae541f. The mutant results (M11 re-measured, M13) are the writer's, recorded on QCLI-572. I did not reproduce them. Runtime claims below come from reasoning about Node, libuv and POSIX behaviour, not from runs.

CHECKS
1. (a3) item 2: implemented as the ruling says.
   - bin/quest.cjs:67-68 is `ownGroup = platform !== "win32" && !isatty(0) && !isatty(1) && !isatty(2)`. The child joins its own group only when none of fds 0, 1 or 2 is a terminal, and stays in the caller's group when any one of them is. That matches the ruling's wording, including Node's tty.isatty.
   - The test the ruling requires is at test:303-319. It runs `: | node wrapper` under script(1), so stdin is a pipe and stdout and stderr are the pty, and it asserts equal pgids.
   - That test fails against the old `!isatty(0)` code: stdin is not a terminal, so the old code puts the child in its own group and the pgids differ. This matches the writer's M13 result: only this test went red.
2. (a2)/(a3) item 1 re-raise set: still matches.
   - NODE_HANDLED at :91 is exactly {SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ, SIGUSR1}.
   - The sequence at :150-158 is unchanged from what the #749 review approved: sweep, then set 128+n, then return early for those three, then remove the listeners and self-kill.
3. F1-F4 and the CHANGELOG nit: see the lines at the end.
4. Can the tests fail? Yes for the fd-0-only mutant. No for the single-clause mutants in finding 1.
5. Orphan prevention: no regression in the code paths.
   - The incident's shape, with all three fds piped, still makes the child its own group (detached), forwards signals to -pid and sweeps the group on exit.
   - The exit-handler sweep, the status passthrough and the sweep before the re-raise are all unchanged.
   - Informational, not a finding: a caller with stdin piped and stdout or stderr on a terminal now leaves the child in the caller's group, so a SIGTERM sent to the wrapper does not reach grandchildren. That is the trade-off (a3) ruled. The code comment (:54-61) and CHANGELOG.md:32-34 both state it.

FINDINGS
1. bin/quest.cjs:67-68 vs test:282-319 — NON-BLOCKING — Neither new clause has its own witness.
   - Remove only `&& !isatty(2)`: both pty tests stay green, because fd 1 is a terminal in the stdin-piped test.
   - Remove only `&& !isatty(1)`: also green, because fd 2 is a terminal there.
   - (a3) requires only the stdin-piped/stdout-on-a-terminal test, so this does not block.
   - Fix: add `: | node wrapper >/dev/null` (only stderr is a terminal; catches the dropped fd-2 clause) and `: | node wrapper 2>/dev/null` (only stdout is a terminal; catches the dropped fd-1 clause).
2. test:386-391 — NON-BLOCKING — The F4 witness is only partly fixed.
   - The new `/inspector/i` and `9229` assertions close the bound-port case: Node's "Starting inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229 failed" line contains both strings.
   - They do not close the timing race. Under M11 the self-kill does not kill the wrapper, so the exit code is still 128+n and the signal is still null. That leaves stderr text as the only witness. If the wrapper exits before the inspector writes anything, all three assertions pass.
   - The comment at :386-388 says "a slow inspector cannot keep a mutant green". That overclaims.
   - A deterministic witness would reuse the ENOEXEC test's --require preload: wrap process.kill and write a marker when it is called with (process.pid, "SIGUSR1").
3. bin/quest.cjs:126-128 — NON-BLOCKING — The F3 caveat states as fact that glibc's execvp retries an ENOEXEC file through /bin/sh. QCLI-572's own implementation note records that diagnosis as inferred, not read from a log, and a green CI on the preload-based test does not confirm it. Suggest "can retry" or "is believed to".
4. test:247-248 — NON-BLOCKING (nit) — A stale comment ("A missing `script` skips this test locally...") sits above `hasScript` and repeats the comment at :271-272, which is the one now attached to ptyTest. Delete the first copy.
5. .quest/tasks/QCLI-572.json — NON-BLOCKING — The task's title, description and five checked ACs still cover only the (a2) #744 findings. No AC covers the (a3) three-fd rule or F1-F4, so closing the task is not gated on the work this PR mainly carries. The implementation notes do record it.

PRIOR FINDINGS AND THE NIT
F1: RESOLVED — bin/quest.cjs:54-61 names QCLI-571 and the grandchild residual when any fd is a terminal, and now says "Off a terminal a plain SIGTERM is fully handled".
F2: RESOLVED — bin/quest.cjs:50-52 states the 128+n exception for SIGPIPE, SIGXFSZ and SIGUSR1 (see NODE_HANDLED).
F3: RESOLVED — bin/quest.cjs:126-128 carries the platform caveat. Finding 3 is about how firmly it is worded.
F4: PARTIAL — the inspector and 9229 assertions were added, which closes the bound-port case. The timing race remains and the comment overclaims (finding 2).
CHANGELOG nit: RESOLVED — CHANGELOG.md:35-37 now reads "Off a terminal, a plain SIGTERM ... is fully handled."
